title: Thrust Lever Detent Seal and Friction Clamp Change on the Centre Pedestal Quadrant

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Change of the thrust lever detent seal and friction clamp after crews reported a soft or missing detent feel at the climb gate, which was traced to lubricant migration past a hardened seal in the quadrant.

sections.reason: Crew reports of a soft or absent detent at the climb gate rose steadily from 2015 and reached one hundred and forty reports in 2017, concentrated on aircraft with more than twenty thousand flight hours. Quadrant strip-downs found the detent lubricant displaced onto the friction clamp faces, which then slipped, so the lever moved without the tactile step the crew expects. The seal that should retain the lubricant was found hardened in every unit examined. The condition is not a control failure, but a detent that cannot be felt is a training and standardisation problem and two operators raised it through their safety boards.
sections.description: The detent seal ASH79119-70 is replaced by a fluorosilicone item with a revised section, and the friction clamp D7610111733252 is replaced by an assembly with a bonded facing that is unaffected by the lubricant. The clamp mounting bracket D7610117147370 is retained but its anchor nuts AGS837365-4E are renewed because the new clamp is thicker at the mounting face. The quadrant is re-lubricated with the revised grease and the detent breakout force is set on the bench before the quadrant is refitted. Work is in zones 211 and 215 with the centre pedestal opened and the throttle quadrant removed. No cable rigging is disturbed and no autothrust interface is changed.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible. No electrical load change. Fully interchangeable. Detent breakout force returns to the design band and is expected to stay there for the life of the aircraft, and the crew report rate should fall to near zero. The quadrant inspection task, the parts figure and the flight crew limitation on manual thrust setting when the autothrust is disconnected all require review, and the throttle friction adjustment procedure is rewritten because the setting method changes.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN Z09624 in February 2019. Retrofit is covered by two bulletins: an in-situ detent force check that can be done on the line, and the quadrant change itself, which needs the pedestal opened and is quoted at ten hours. Kits are shipped as a complete quadrant exchange to avoid a bench set-up at the operator.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z09624 within the normal quadrant supply
